name: Massachusetts
overview: A refundable senior circuit breaker covers qualifying homeowners and renters; it is distinct from locally administered property-tax exemptions.

programs.name: Senior Circuit Breaker Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: At least one eligible taxpayer must be 65 or older by the end of the tax year.
programs.incomeDefinition: Massachusetts adjusted gross income with statutory additions and subtractions; excludes specified personal exemptions.
programs.incomeLimits: 2025 total income: $75,000 single, $94,000 head of household, $112,000 joint; married filing separately is ineligible.
programs.formulaSummary: Credit qualifying housing payments above 10% of program income, limited to the annual maximum. Owner expenses include property taxes after reductions and half of separately stated water/sewer charges. Renters use 25% of annual qualifying rent.
programs.application: File Schedule CB with the Massachusetts income-tax return; a return is required even when no tax would otherwise be due.
eligibilityNotes: 2025 assessed-value ceiling for homeowners is $1,298,000, before residential exemptions and after abatements.
Dependents, nonresidents, subsidized renters and tenants of tax-exempt property are excluded.
interactions: Subtract property-tax abatements, exemptions and other reductions when measuring owner payments.
programs.programYear: Tax year 2025; claimed with the return filed in 2026.

sources.title: 2025 tax tips for seniors and retirees

researchNotes: The legal household income definition differs from federal AGI.
Locally administered exemptions are context, not an additional statewide cash credit. The inventory does not enumerate every municipal option.
